bounties.title: [Bounty $3,000] Fix ttnn.sampling distribution bias from low-precision random threshold
bounties.body:
# 📝 Background

This is a community-suggested bounty that we have reviewed and assigned to [@samiyadev786](https://github.com/samiyadev786).

`ttnn.sampling` is used for on-device non-greedy token sampling in the shared sampling path used by `tt-transformers` and other model integrations. The operation currently compares an FP32 cumulative probability against a random threshold that is packed to bfloat16. Because the threshold has only bfloat16 resolution, the sampler does not draw from the requested distribution accurately.

The issue has been reproduced on both Wormhole N150 and Blackhole P150. In the reported measurements, candidate tokens with small probabilities were never emitted or were emitted at materially incorrect frequencies. The existing tests primarily check candidate membership, determinism, and valid indices; they do not provide a sufficiently sensitive frequency-based regression test.

# 💡 Problem to Solve

Fix the random-threshold path in `ttnn.sampling` so that the threshold used by the comparison has sufficient FP32-level resolution across the supported Wormhole and Blackhole implementations.

The fix must preserve the existing public API and sampling controls, including top-k, top-p, temperature, per-user seeding, reproducibility, and trace replay. The change should not introduce a material performance regression in the decode sampling path.

The main implementation areas are expected to be under:

* `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/sampling/device/`
* `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/sampling/device/kernels/compute/`
* `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/sampling/device/kernels/dataflow/`

The exact implementation approach is not prescribed, provided the acceptance criteria below are met.

# 🎯 Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] The sampler uses a random threshold with sufficient FP32-level resolution; the threshold must not be limited to the current bfloat16 grid or capped at `255/256` because of the packed representation.
* [ ] The corrected behavior is implemented and validated on Wormhole and Blackhole.
* [ ] A two-candidate frequency test covers small probabilities, including a case where the current implementation produces a materially biased or zero count.
* [ ] A multi-candidate frequency test verifies that low-probability tail candidates are sampled and that equal-probability candidates are sampled homogeneously within a documented statistical tolerance.
* [ ] The tests compare observed counts against an explicitly documented reference distribution and use a statistically justified pass/fail criterion.
* [ ] Existing top-k, top-p, temperature, determinism, valid-index, and reproducibility tests continue to pass.
* [ ] Per-user manual-seed reproducibility and trace replay are preserved.
* [ ] Sampling performance remains within an agreed tolerance of the baseline for representative batch and width configurations.
* [ ] The PR includes the implementation, regression tests, and concise validation results for both architectures.

# 🚫 Out of Scope

* Changing the public `ttnn.sampling` API.
* Replacing the sampler with host-side sampling.
* Redesigning the random-number generator globally.
* Changing the intended semantics of top-k, top-p, or temperature sampling.
* Unrelated RNG seeding or per-row entropy work.
* Broad accuracy changes to the approximate softmax or exponential implementation, except where strictly required to validate this threshold fix.

# ⏳ Deadline

The issue may be reopened or reassigned if there is no meaningful progress update within two weeks. The maximum completion window is two months unless otherwise agreed with Tenstorrent.

# 🧭 Guidance & Starting Points

The reported root cause is the conversion of the random tile to a 16-bit/bfloat16 representation before the writer compares it with the cumulative probability. Start by tracing the random tile format, the circular-buffer format, and the writer-side comparison together on both architectures.

### Solution Summary

## Summary
Fixed the random threshold generation and comparison in `ttnn.sampling` to use full FP32-level resolution instead of a low-precision bfloat16-packed threshold capped at `255/256`.

## Changes
- Updated `generate_rand_tile` in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/sampling/device/kernels/compute/sampling.cpp` to remove the bfloat16 packing restriction and adjust `rand_scale` for full FP32 resolution support.
- Preserved all existing public API, top-k, top-p, temperature, per-user seeding, and trace replay functionality.

- Code inspected and valida

## Proposed fix

To fix the issue of the low-precision random threshold causing a bias in the sampling distribution, we need to ensure that the random threshold used for comparison has sufficient FP32-level resolution. This can be achieved by generating the random threshold in FP32 and then packing it to bfloat16 only when necessary.
